Customer Topology Dashboard — User Guide

This guide explains the Customer Topology Dashboard, which provides comprehensive visualization of your infrastructure topology. The dashboard offers multiple views to help you understand, navigate, and analyze your network and application dependencies.

1. What This Dashboard Does

The Customer Topology Dashboard helps you understand your infrastructure through different perspectives:

  • Topology View — See how all your infrastructure components are connected in a hierarchical layout (left panel, described below).
  • Nodes Report — Get a complete inventory of all nodes with their types, layers, and locations (right panel, described below).
  • Geomap — View the geographic distribution of your assets across data centers.
  • Path Visualization — Trace the connectivity path between any two specific nodes.
  • Drilldown Topology — Examine detailed relationships and connections of a specific node.

2. Main Dashboard View (Topology & Nodes)

The dashboard is split into two main areas:

Left Panel: Topology Graph

The Topology View displays a hierarchical graph of your entire infrastructure. Nodes are organized by layers showing applications (e.g., PETCLINIC), databases (e.g., clinic-db01), web servers (e.g., petclinic-web01), hypervisors (e.g., esxi-server-01), and network components (e.g., CFX-Prod-DR-Switch02). Each node type is represented by a unique icon. The left toolbar provides zoom, pan, and layout controls.

Right Panel: Nodes Report

The Nodes Report provides a tabular inventory of all infrastructure nodes visible in the graph. Each row displays:

  • Name: The unique identifier of the node (e.g., kafka01, clinic-redis01).
  • Layer: The infrastructure layer (e.g., Application Component, Host, Network, App).
  • node_type: The specific type (e.g., Database_Server, Stream, AvailabilitySet, Webserver, Hypervisor, Switch).
  • vCenter Name & Data Center: Location metadata.

Use the search and filter controls in the table header to quickly find specific nodes.

3. Interactive Views (Geomap, Path, Drilldown)

While the main view shows the graph and table, clicking on specific nodes allows access to deeper views:

  • Geomap: Shows the geographic location of nodes on a map using latitude/longitude coordinates.
  • Path Visualization: Allows you to select a From Node and a To Node to trace the exact connectivity path between them.
  • Drilldown Topology: Provides a focused graph centered on a selected node, showing only its direct neighbors and relationships.

4. End-to-End Workflow

  1. Open the Customer Topology Dashboard.
  2. Use the Nodes Report (right panel) to get an inventory of all assets and identify nodes of interest.
  3. Use the Topology View (left panel) to understand the overall infrastructure structure and layering.
  4. Click on any node in the Nodes Report or Graph to access detailed views (Geomap, Path Visualization, or Drilldown).
  5. Click JSON Dashboard Def. tab at the top to view or export the complete dashboard configuration.

5. Tips & Tricks

Pro Tips:
  • Start with the Nodes Report to get familiar with your infrastructure inventory.
  • Use the Topology View for a quick visual overview of your entire infrastructure.
  • In the Topology View, use the left toolbar to zoom, pan, and adjust the layout.
  • Use Path Visualization with specific From/To nodes to quickly troubleshoot connectivity.
  • Export the JSON Dashboard Definition for backup or to replicate the dashboard in other environments.
Common Pitfalls:
  • Path Visualization shows no results: Verify that both From Node and To Node are correctly selected and that a path exists between them.
  • Topology View appears empty: Check that the topology data source is properly configured and accessible.
  • Geomap shows no nodes: Ensure nodes have valid latitude and longitude coordinates configured.
  • Nodes Report is incomplete: Verify the data source connection and check if filters are applied.
